title: optimize-prefetch-pipeline-with-windowed-chunking-and-priority-scheduler
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: We observed persistent tail-latency and unit-cost regressions on mixed-length workloads when the prefill stage processed very long prefixes before decode began. This change introduces a windowed prefetch (chunking) approach and a lightweight priority scheduler to better overlap prefetch/prefill work with decode, plus adaptive KV warmup hints to reduce cold-KV misses. Design summary: 1) Windowed chunking: instead of submitting an entire prefill sequence in one go, the prefetch manager breaks the prefill into bounded window chunks (configurable window_size and lookahead). This enables earlier decode tokens to start while later prefix tokens are still being prefetched. 2) Priority scheduler: a low-overhead priority queue assigns higher weight to windows that unblock decode (near-decode boundary), so short-critical-path chunks are scheduled earlier. The scheduler is pluggable and falls back to the existing round-robin policy when disabled. 3) Adaptive KV warmup hints: prefetchers emit KV warmup hints for likely-attended KV pages based on recent attention patterns; KV manager probabilistically warms those pages into the local cache during idle cycles. 4) Continuous batching compatibility: the chunking strategy integrates with continuous-batching by tagging chunked requests with a chunk_id and preserving token-order semantics in the batching layer. Implementation: changes span runtime/pipeline/prefetch_manager.cc (new chunking logic and config), runtime/scheduler/priority_scheduler.cc (new scheduler thread and queue), runtime/kv/kv_warmup_manager.cc (statistics and warmup task), runtime/batching/batch_tagging.h (chunk_id header), and tests/perf/prefetch_window_bench.cc. The diff separates algorithmic changes (chunking/scheduling) from I/O/serialization work; kernel selection logic gets a small hint flag so that decode kernels can prefer low-latency kernels for early windows. Checklist: - [x] Implement windowed chunking and chunk metadata propagation - [x] Add priority scheduler with pluggable policy - [x] Wire KV warmup hinting and safe no-op when KV warmup disabled - [x] End-to-end unit and integration tests - [x] Microbenchmarks and canary rollout plan Performance: on internal perf-lab mixed-length trace (50% short/50% long) we measured median latency down 9%, p95 down 18%, p99 down 24%, overall throughput +11% under balanced load, and per-token GPU time down ~8% due to fewer KV stalls. Short-request tail latency saw the largest uplift (because early windows unblock decode). Rollout and safety: feature gated by runtime config flags: prefetch.windowed.enabled, scheduler.priority.enabled, kv.warmup.enabled. Canary rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated regression checks (latency, error-rate, token cost). Automatic fallback: if p95 increases by >10% vs baseline the canary auto-rolls back. Backwards compatibility: chunk_id is opaque metadata internal to the runtime; no changes to public API. Migration notes: disabled by default in release branch; enabled on dedicated clusters under ENG-2218 for initial stress testing. Testing: unit tests for chunk boundary correctness, scheduler fairness tests, KV warmup heatmap assertions, and multiple long-running perf runs on perf-canary infra. Related work and references: this PR complements recent speculative-prefetch prototypes by adding a deterministic windowed overlap path and explicit priority scheduling (see ENG-2275 for design notes). We intentionally did not modify large decode kernels; instead we added a kernel-selection hint to prefer low-latency kernels for early windows which avoids a heavy kernel churn. Known limitations: the adaptive KV warmup is probabilistic and may waste work on extremely random attention patterns; we included a conservative decay to avoid sustained warmup cost. Future improvements: learnable window sizing per-customer workload, tighter integration with per-model kernel profiles, and a scheduler-observed backpressure signal to dynamically shrink windows. Documentation: added config docs and an operations checklist in docs/ops/prefetching.md.
commits: feat(prefetch): windowed chunking for prefetch manager
feat(scheduler): add lightweight priority scheduler and policy interface
perf(kv): adaptive kv warmup hints and warmup manager
chore(tests): add perf benchmarks for windowed prefetch traces
docs: op guide and rollout playbook for windowed prefetch
review_comments: Maya Singh: Can we ensure that chunking doesn't increase memory pressure under large batch sizes? Suggested adding a high-water mark and an early-drop metric. Ethan: Added high_water_limit config and unit tests; documented the metric.
Jules Carter: Priority scheduler looks good but request fairness must be guaranteed. Please add starvation protection. Ethan: Implemented aging-based boost and added scheduler fairness test.
Liam O'Neill: CI failed on macOS build due to an include order; minor fix pushed. CI passes after re-run. Liam: Approved after green CI.
Ops (Riley): Add rollback playbook for canary; ensure KV warmup can be disabled cluster-wide. Ethan: Playbook added to docs and config flag present.
release_notes: Introduce windowed prefetch chunking and a priority scheduler to improve tail latency and throughput for mixed-length workloads. Includes adaptive KV warmup hints and continuous-batching compatibility. Feature is feature-gated; rollout via canary with automatic rollback on regressions.
